1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nf3 b6 4.g3 Ba6 5.b3.strategy: Blocks the check with the bishop, the safe way. Blocking with the knight loses material to ...Bc3. The bishop can later go to c3 to challenge the long diagonal, though it then blocks the c-file for White's own rook.

Retreats to e7, having forced White's bishop to d2, where it stands in the way of White's own development. Black prepares a central break from a solid position and goes on to equalise, in the main line of this modern system.
1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nf3 b6 4.g3 Ba6 5.b3.name: Queen's Indian Defence: Fianchetto Variation, Check Variation, Intermezzo Line

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nf3 b6 4.g3 Ba6 5.b3.strategy: Defends the bishop on b4 with the queen, so Black keeps it there and keeps the option to trade it for White's bishop on d2. A more ambitious approach than the retreat: it keeps the tension, though the queen on e7 takes the bishop's retreat square.
